name: Polyploidy Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Cytogenetic Diagnostic Criteria for Polyploidy Syndrome

criteria.description: Detection of triploid or tetraploid karyotype in peripheral blood or tissue samples
Severe intrauterine growth retardation or postnatal growth failure
Presence of characteristic craniofacial abnormalities including micrognathia and hypertelorism
Presence of multiple congenital malformations affecting various organ systems
Ultrasound evidence of polyploidy-associated anomalies such as hydatidiform mole or fetal demise

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Cytogenetic confirmation of polyploidy plus at least one major clinical feature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily confirmed by cytogenetic analysis; clinical features support suspicion.

searchTerms: abnormal placental growth called hydatidiform mole
molar pregnancy with placental tissue changes
split lip and/or roof of mouth
spinal cord and brain tube defects

occasional.symptomName: Respiratory distress due to pulmonary hypoplasia
searchTerms: respiratory distress due to lung underdevelopment
poor lung growth causing breathing problems
hormone problems including low thyroid function

laboratory: Karyotype analysis showing triploidy (69,XXX; 69,XXY; 69,XYY) or tetraploidy (92,XXXX)
Elevated serum hCG in cases with hydatidiform mole
imaging: Prenatal ultrasound showing growth retardation, molar changes in placenta, and multiple congenital anomalies
Postnatal MRI or CT revealing brain malformations or neural tube defects
genetic: Presence of an entire extra set(s) of chromosomes in all or some cells
No single gene mutation; chromosomal numerical abnormality
other: Placental pathology consistent with partial or complete hydatidiform mole
Fetal demise or stillbirth common in polyploidy pregnancies

distinguishingFeatures: Triploidy is a form of polyploidy but often presents with distinct karyotype and clinical features
May have different survival outcomes and specific malformations
Presence of two or more cell lines with different karyotypes
Clinical features may be milder or variable compared to full polyploidy

redFlags: Severe intrauterine growth retardation with multiple congenital anomalies
Hydatidiform mole detected on placental examination
Karyotype revealing triploid or tetraploid chromosomal complement
references: Gardner RJM, Sutherland GR. Chromosome Abnormalities and Genetic Counseling. 4th Edition. Oxford University Press; 2012.
Nussbaum RL, McInnes RR, Willard HF. Thompson & Thompson Genetics in Medicine. 8th Edition. Elsevier; 2015.
